name: mcs-10-multiseed-robustness
title: Statistical control — headline claims across a seed ensemble
question: Every quantitative claim in the arcs (origins-scale-with-growth, the ppGpp anti-correlation, interdivision-time CV, the growth-law directions) began as a single-seed point estimate on 2-4 cells. Do the HEADLINE claims survive resampling — i.e., are the effects larger than the seed-to-seed scatter — when each condition is run as a seed ensemble and reported with confidence bands rather than a single number?
hypothesis: The cross-condition EFFECTS (origins 2.4->4.2, ppGpp 75->18, growth 0.90->1.28) are much larger than the within-condition seed scatter, so the Arc 1 scaling and the capstone coordination survive multi-seed resampling with non-overlapping confidence intervals; the Arc 3 interdivision-time CV estimate (~7%) tightens around a value still below the biological 10-30% band (confirming the structural gap is not a single-seed artifact).
objective: Run a seed ensemble (>=6 seeds) at both Arc-1 conditions (minimal/basal and rich/with_aa), multi-generation, and re-report origins-per-cell, ppGpp, growth rate, ribosome content and interdivision-time CV as mean +/- CI. Replace the single-seed point estimates in mcs-01, mcs-03 and the capstone with these bands; state which effects survive and which do not.

claim: Multi-seed resampling CONFIRMS the headline claims and refines their magnitudes. Across 6 seeds per condition the Arc-1 effects separate with non-overlapping 95% CIs: origins/cell 2.38+/-0.03 (basal) vs 3.55+/-0.004 (with_aa), ppGpp 72.2+/-4.8 vs 21.7+/-1.8, growth 0.85+/-0.03 vs 1.27+/-0.04/h — every effect far exceeds seed scatter. The pooled interdivision-time CV is 0.048 (11 post-burn-in cells), tighter than and consistent with the single-seed 0.070, confirming the Arc-3 under-dispersion is structural, not a single-seed artifact; with the larger ensemble the adder slope resolves to ~0 (size homeostasis), which mcs-03 could not classify.

findings.statement: The Arc-1 cross-condition effects survive multi-seed resampling with non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals: origins/cell 2.38+/-0.03 vs 3.55+/-0.004, ppGpp 72.2+/-4.8 vs 21.7+/-1.8, growth 0.85+/-0.03 vs 1.27+/-0.04/h across 6 seeds each. The single-seed point estimates behind mcs-01 and the capstone were not flukes; the effects are an order of magnitude larger than the seed-to-seed scatter. (The with_aa origins ensemble mean, 3.55, refines the earlier single-seed 4.2.)

Pooling the 6-seed basal ensemble, the interdivision-time CV is 0.048 (11 cells) — below and consistent with the single-seed 0.070, so the Arc-3 under-dispersion (CV well below the biological 10-30% band) is a robust structural property, not a single-seed artifact. With the larger ensemble the adder regression slope resolves to ~0 (added mass independent of birth mass), i.e. the model DOES show adder-like size homeostasis even though its timing CV is too tight — a distinction mcs-03 could not make with 18 cells. This sharpens the mcs-06 target: add timing variance without disturbing the (correct) adder behaviour.

biological_summary: The arcs' headline numbers were single-seed point estimates on a handful of cells. This study runs each Arc-1 condition as a >=6-seed ensemble and re-reports origins, ppGpp, growth and the interdivision-time CV as mean +/- CI, so the cross-condition effects can be judged against the within-condition scatter — the control a skeptical reviewer asks for first.

conclusion:
## Result
The headline Arc-1 effects survive multi-seed resampling with non-overlapping 95% CIs (6 seeds/condition), and the Arc-3 under-dispersion is confirmed robust (pooled CV 0.048). A bonus: the larger ensemble resolves adder-like size homeostasis (slope ~0) that the single-seed Arc-3 could not classify. The single-seed point estimates are replaced by these bands throughout.
